vendors.revenue_share_model: Custom / negotiated. SaaS platforms using Stripe Connect are eligible for a 'revenue sharing' program on processing volume; Premier Partner (SaaS track) requires at least $1M in partnership revenue for buy-rate platforms or $300M in payment volume for referral-model platforms. Services-track partners earn referral/co-sell support rather than disclosed percentages. Exact rev-share percentages are not publicly disclosed. ([Stripe SaaS platform partners docs](https://docs.stripe.com/partners/platforms))
vendors.fx_markup_transparency: Not publicly detailed for partners. Stripe discloses over 125+ global payment methods and currency support in its core payments docs, but does not publish standardized FX markup disclosure requirements for partners or end-customers on its partner pages. ([Stripe Sessions 2025 product update](https://stripe.com/blog/top-product-updates-sessions-2025))
vendors.cross_border_coverage: 135+ currencies accepted and 40+ countries with full Stripe account support. The October 2026 update adds instant stablecoin payouts to 160 markets and stablecoin card issuing in 27 EU countries, bringing availability to 65+ countries worldwide; Stripe plans to expand card issuing to 100 countries by year-end 2026. The source does not state that the planned 100-country expansion is already live. ([Stripe supported currencies](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies); [Stripe October 2026 update](https://stripe.com/blog/new-ways-for-fintechs-to-move-money-and-expand-globally))
vendors.embedded_finance_capabilities: Yes. Connect, Treasury, Issuing, and Global Payouts can be combined for platform-fintech products. Global Payouts can be embedded through hosted forms or APIs; the October 2026 update adds stablecoin-funded card programs using custodial or noncustodial wallets or Stripe financial accounts, with automatic local-currency conversion at purchase. ([Stripe October 2026 update](https://stripe.com/blog/new-ways-for-fintechs-to-move-money-and-expand-globally); [Stripe OUSD launch](https://stripe.com/newsroom/news/ousd-is-now-available-on-stripe))
vendors.api_first: Yes. Stripe's entire partner ecosystem is built around API integration (Payment Intents, Connect, Checkout, Payment Element, webhooks). ([Stripe SaaS platform partners docs](https://docs.stripe.com/partners/platforms))
vendors.deal_registration: Yes. Services-track Partner and Premier Partner tiers both have 'Deal registration to request co-selling support' as a stated benefit. ([Stripe Services partners docs](https://docs.stripe.com/partners/services))
vendors.mdf_available: Yes. Both Partner and Premier tiers in the Services track are eligible to request market development funds (MDF); Premier Partners in the SaaS track get MDF as an added benefit. ([Stripe Services partners docs](https://docs.stripe.com/partners/services); [Stripe SaaS platform partners docs](https://docs.stripe.com/partners/platforms))
vendors.annual_partner_fee: No standard published fee for the core Partner Ecosystem; one third-party affiliate resource cites a legacy 'Stripe Verified Partner Program' with a $250/year fee, but this is not corroborated on Stripe's current official pages. ([Wise blog on Stripe affiliate program](https://wise.com/gb/blog/stripe-affiliate-program))
vendors.ecosystem_size: Not disclosed as a specific partner count on official pages; described as 'thousands of trusted partners around the world.' ([Stripe Partner Ecosystem page](https://stripe.com/partners))

recent_program_changes.change: Stripe announced instant stablecoin payouts to recipients in 160 markets, available from the Dashboard and through Global Payouts hosted forms or APIs. It also announced stablecoin card issuing in 27 EU countries, bringing availability to more than 65 countries worldwide, with 100 countries planned by year-end 2026. Cards can draw from custodial or noncustodial wallets or Stripe financial accounts; local-currency conversion occurs at purchase.

Stripe agreed to acquire Parafin, an embedded financial products platform that provides small-business credit through platform partners. Parafin offers capital, Pay Over Time, and Spend products; the acquisition is proposed and expected to close in the coming months, subject to customary conditions including any required regulatory clearances.

Stripe partnered with Open Standard to launch Open USD (OUSD) across Stripe products, making OUSD the default stablecoin configuration on Tempo. Businesses can hold OUSD in Treasury, use Issuing stablecoin cards, accept OUSD with Payments, use Bridge orchestration and Privy wallets, and send OUSD to crypto wallets in 100+ countries; Ramp stablecoin accounts are a named use case. Open Standard partner rewards are available, but no reward or revenue-share rate is disclosed.

BLIK expanded its Stripe partnership through Stripe Dynamic Payment Methods: Stripe merchants in more than 30 countries can offer Polish shoppers BLIK without building a separate payment-provider integration. No new currency or corridor was named.

Stripe launched Treasury in Australia, giving businesses one platform to accept payments, hold and convert funds, and pay recipients in nearly 100 countries; Australian businesses can hold AUD, USD, GBP, and EUR and convert between 10 supported currencies, including HKD, SGD, and NZD.

Stripe and DBS announced a strategic partnership for cross-border payments and agentic commerce in Asia: Stripe will use DBS money-movement and cash-management capabilities, while DBS will explore Stripe's programmable financial services and embedded-finance platform for institutional clients; the companies will also explore joint agentic-AI capabilities.

Stripe powered Ramp stablecoin Bill Pay and Stablecoin Accounts through Bridge and Privy, enabling bank-funded stablecoin payments and 24/7 stablecoin balances/payments for businesses, including global supplier payments.

Stripe Sessions 2026 added Treasury and platform capabilities: storage in 15 currencies for US/UK businesses by year-end, stablecoin support for 41 additional markets, noncustodial-wallet-backed cross-border movement in 150+ markets, and marketplace stablecoin rails for seller payouts in 100 additional countries.

Stripe restructured the Partner Ecosystem into a streamlined two-tier model (Stripe Partner and Premier Partner) across four tracks (Services, SaaS platforms, Apps, Payment methods), raising baseline standards for technical expertise, business impact, and customer success.
Seven new partner specializations launched: Agentic Commerce, Radar, Terminal, Retail, Media, Financial Services, and Travel & Hospitality.

Launch of the Stripe Partner Solutions Program, moving partners from custom implementations to repeatable industry solutions on a 70/30 prebuilt-to-customizable model; partners on this model reportedly grew revenue 20% faster year-over-year.

At Stripe Sessions 2025, Stripe previewed Stripe Orchestration (multi-processor management), announced Managed Payments (merchant-of-record offering), and expanded to 125+ global payment methods including stablecoins and real-time rails like Pix and UPI.

recent_program_changes.change: Adyen and Sabre announced an integration embedding Adyen Terminal API payments in Sabre's Electronic Payment Gateway and Mosaic Digital Workspace Air, supporting airport check-in and airline ancillary sales such as baggage and seat upgrades. The release names airlines using Sabre's airport front-end as the target; it does not specify a new country rollout.

Adyen announced a strategic partnership with Danish fintech Flatpay, providing acquiring and unified global financial infrastructure as Flatpay expands beyond its seven European markets. Flatpay may integrate Adyen Embedded Finance features including instant settlement, cash advances, business accounts, and card issuing; these are optional capabilities with no launch date stated.

Adyen added Wero to its platform across France, Belgium, Luxembourg, Germany, the Netherlands, and Austria, covering real-time A2A payments, refunds, disputes, and chargebacks and supporting the gradual iDEAL-to-Wero transition in the Netherlands.

Adyen completed its acquisitions of loyalty/incentives platform Talon.One and enterprise billing platform Orb after regulatory and customary approvals; integration of Talon.One's promotional engine and Orb's flexible billing began.

Adyen launched Adyen Agentic, a modular API suite (Agentic Feed, Agentic Cart, Agentic Payments) for selling through conversational AI; initial availability is limited to US enterprise merchants with global expansion planned.

Adyen launched an enhanced, tiered Partner Program (Technology and Service partner tracks) with clearer engagement models, revenue-sharing eligibility for technology partners, and MDF for top-tier partners.

Adyen detailed the new Partner Program structure, including Premier and Premier Plus tiers, bi-annual product roadmap access for Premier Partners, and partner badges tied to job-to-be-done categories.
Sokin and Adyen announced a strategic global partnership giving US businesses a single solution for e-commerce payments and treasury operations.
Adyen expanded Dynamic Currency Conversion to support 25 additional currencies.

recent_program_changes.change: Airwallex went live as a payment provider for OpenTable restaurants in the United States and Canada, supporting deposits and prepaid dining Experiences. Australia and Mexico are identified as planned expansion markets, not current availability.

Airwallex's October release added multi-currency liquidity pools and per-connected-account spending limits for platforms, plus an agent-managed Business Accounts experience under user-set permissions and approvals. It also added Portugal's MB WAY, Malaysian MYR local transfers via DuitNow ID/RENTAS, and Australian AUD local payouts above A$10 million through NPP and BECS; its Agentic Commerce Suite is in early access globally.

Airwallex described work to add stablecoin support in regulated markets and said it had invested to incubate Metal, becoming its first design partner. This is a development strategy, not a launched customer product; the page does not specify a launch date or eligible markets.

Airwallex announced it had acquired South Korean payments company Paynuri, including its Payment Gateway and Prepaid Electronic Payment Instrument licenses and foreign-exchange registration. Global business accounts and payment acquiring were described as the first planned Korean launches; the announcement presents the acquisition as completed.

Airwallex September product updates added Billing Direct Debit via ACH, SEPA, Bacs, and EFT, API payouts to PayPal Wallets, and transaction-currency card spend limits across 85+ currencies; structured e-invoicing for French businesses was also introduced in early access. These extend embedded billing and payout rails; the update did not announce a new stablecoin capability or country corridor.

Airwallex and Affirm added Affirm pay-over-time checkout for eligible US shoppers: merchants based in 35 countries can offer four interest-free installments or monthly plans through Airwallex without a separate integration.

Airwallex began supporting Wero through its direct EPI partnership: eligible merchants globally can accept Wero without a European entity; Germany and Belgium are live, France is slated for October 2026, and a Shopify plugin is available.
BBCIncorp honored with Airwallex 'Outstanding Partner Award 2025', highlighting active partner recognition programs.
Airwallex continues to segment its partner program into five named tracks: Corporate services, Agencies, Technology partners, Startup ecosystem, and Affiliates.

vendors.revenue_share_model: Custom / negotiated for embedding partners (banks, enterprises, platforms); not structured as a public partner rev-share/tier program like Stripe or Adyen. Wise's own end-customer pricing is transparent: average fee of 0.53% globally as of December 2025, down from 0.59% a year earlier, using the mid-market rate with zero FX markup. ([Wise December 2025 fee review](https://wise.com/us/blog/december-fee-review-2025); [FXC Intelligence Wise investor day insights](https://www.fxcintel.com/research/reports/ct-wise-2025-investor-day))
vendors.fx_markup_transparency: Yes — Wise's core differentiator. Wise uses the real mid-market exchange rate with 0% markup and charges a separate, transparent fee (fixed + variable, ~0.33%-0.65% depending on corridor) disclosed upfront before every transfer; this transparency extends to Wise Platform's embedded offering for partner banks/enterprises. ([Wise mid-market rate explainer](https://wise.com/gb/blog/mid-market-rate-explained); [Wise December 2025 fee review](https://wise.com/us/blog/december-fee-review-2025))
vendors.cross_border_coverage: Wise's current Platform page states coverage in 200+ countries and 110+ currencies, replacing the tracker's older 160+ countries / 40+ currencies snapshot. Recent integrations include OakNorth for UK business payments in 20+ currencies and Vivid Business for payments in 40+ currencies, with CNY payouts already live across 27 European countries. ([Wise Platform](https://wise.com/platform/); [Wise/OakNorth](https://newsroom.wise.com/en-UKI/272966-oaknorth-selects-wise-platform-to-power-international-payments-for-uk-businesses/); [Wise/Vivid](https://newsroom.wise.com/en-CEU/273296-vivid-selects-wise-platform-for-international-payments-for-smes/))
vendors.embedded_finance_capabilities: Yes. Wise Platform lets banks, enterprises, and platforms embed send/receive money, card issuing, multi-currency accounts, customizable onboarding/KYC, and Swift messaging integration via the Wise Platform API. ([Wise Platform page](https://wise.com/platform/))
vendors.api_first: Yes. Wise Platform explicitly offers connection 'via Swift or API' with full API documentation for partners. ([Wise Platform page](https://wise.com/platform/))
vendors.deal_registration: Not publicly disclosed (Wise Platform is a direct enterprise/bank partnership model rather than a classic channel-partner program).
vendors.annual_partner_fee: Not publicly disclosed; embedding partners negotiate commercial terms directly with Wise.
vendors.ecosystem_size: 70+ licenses worldwide; 950+ engineers; Wise FY26 added Platform partners including UniCredit, Raiffeisen Bank, MBSB Bank, and Capitec; Q2 2026 expanded Raiffeisen Bank International and GoTyme Bank partnerships and added Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo. ([Wise Platform page](https://wise.com/platform/); [Wise FY26 results](https://owners.wise.com/news-releases/news-release-details/wise-group-plc-reports-full-year-2026-financial-results); [Wise Platform Q2 2026 update](https://wise.com/gb/blog/wise-platform-mission-update-q2-2026))

recent_program_changes.change: Vivid selected Wise Platform for international payments for SME customers. The announcement says Vivid Business supports payments in 40+ currencies and that CNY payouts are already live across 27 European countries; other currencies are planned.

OakNorth selected Wise Platform to provide international payments for UK business customers with annual turnover of £1 million to £100 million. The announcement cites payments in more than 20 currencies, 77% arriving in under 20 seconds, and the mid-market rate with the cost shown transparently.

MBSB Bank expanded its Wise Platform-powered Global Easy Transfer service from 12 to 20 currencies, adding the Vietnamese dong, Canadian dollar, and UAE dirham. The service is available through the bank’s MJourney app and web platform; transfers display costs upfront and support real-time tracking.

Wise Platform expanded its Raiffeisen Bank International partnership and its GoTyme Bank partnership in the Philippines; GoTyme launched Send Money Abroad powered by Wise Platform for transfers to 160+ countries, and Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo joined the Wise Platform partner network.

Wise FY26 results reported two new direct domestic-payment connections in Brazil and Japan, new licenses in South Africa, the UAE, and Thailand, new Wise Platform partners UniCredit, Raiffeisen Bank, MBSB Bank, and Capitec (April 2026), and Assets launched in Brazil.
Wise's December 2025 fee review confirmed the average global fee fell to 0.53%, the lowest in 5 years, and moved to a single all-inclusive upfront fee to eliminate hidden costs.
Wise Platform showcased embedding low-cost, instant cross-border payments into banks and ecosystems at Sibos 2025.
Wise reported FY26 cross-border volume growth of 25% to £181.7bn, while deliberately cutting its take rate to 51 basis points in Q4.
Wise Platform published a quarterly product update covering new integrations and platform capabilities.

Nium and Coinbase launched a live USDC integration across Nium's 40+ licenses and 190+ countries, enabling clients to fund payouts in USDC, settle in USDC or fiat, convert stablecoins to fiat, and launch USDC-backed card programs with less prefunding.
Nium and Emirates NBD expanded their strategic partnership (first unveiled 2024), extending real-time payouts across Emirates NBD Group in the UAE with exploration of expansion to Saudi Arabia.

Circle and Nium partnered to bring USDC settlement to Nium's cross-border payments network spanning 190+ countries.

dLocal Ghana Limited secured an Enhanced Payment Service Provider license from the Bank of Ghana, establishing a basis for direct operation of digital payments in Ghana under local regulation and supporting local methods such as mobile money and bank transfers. The announcement did not specify a new currency or cross-border corridor launch.

dLocal launched dMoRe, a Merchant of Record solution for global SaaS, gaming, and ecommerce businesses entering emerging markets; dLocal takes on local legal, tax, and compliance responsibilities and runs the service on its payment rails across 60+ emerging markets, shortening launch timelines to weeks.

dLocal expanded BNPL Fuse to emerging-market coverage spanning 500M buyers, with live coverage in Argentina, Mexico, Brazil, Egypt, South Africa, Saudi Arabia, and Malaysia; Colombia, Chile, and the UAE are in the pipeline.

dLocal partnered with Stable Sea to enable low-cost B2B cross-border payments using stablecoin rails while routing payouts through dLocal's local infrastructure across 40+ countries.
dLocal's partner page confirms current scale: 60+ countries, 1,000+ local payment methods, and 760+ merchants, reflecting continued expansion in emerging markets.

([Payoneer integration partnerships page](https://www.payoneer.com/integration-partnerships/); [Payoneer Q4/FY2025 results](https://investor.payoneer.com/news-releases/news-release-details/payoneer-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-financial))

recent_program_changes.change: Payoneer Canada Limited registered with the Bank of Canada as a payment service provider under the Retail Payment Activities Act, supporting its continued provision of regulated payment services and local-currency collection in Canada.

Payoneer's current Integration Partnerships page documents four public tiers: Registered, Silver, Gold, and Platinum. Silver and Gold describe enhanced commissions and milestone bonuses; Platinum describes custom revenue share. The page does not publish exact rates, numerical thresholds, or a specific program launch date.

Payoneer stockholders approved the proposed Nuvei merger agreement at the September 14 special meeting. The SEC filing records 224,985,441 votes in favor; approval was a key milestone, not closing. The transaction remains pending regulatory and other merger conditions; Payoneer has not yet become a Nuvei subsidiary.

Payoneer secured a license to operate in Israel under the Regulation of Payment Services and Payment Initiation Act, enabling collection of funds, holding balances, and making payments in Israel for local businesses and international businesses with Israeli counterparties.

Payoneer filed a definitive proxy for the pending Nuvei acquisition and scheduled a virtual stockholder meeting for September 14, 2026. The $2.75B transaction still requires Payoneer stockholder and regulatory approvals and had not closed; Payoneer remains independent until closing.

Payoneer's DEFA14A materials confirmed the Nuvei acquisition remains pending: shareholder approval and regulatory clearances are still required, an estimated shareholder vote is expected around August–September 2026, closing remains estimated for mid-2027, and Payoneer remains independent and Nasdaq-listed until closing.

Nuvei announced a definitive agreement to acquire Payoneer for $2.75 billion ($7.40/share cash), creating a combined platform for local and cross-border commerce projected to generate ~$3B in annual revenue and process $500B+ in volume across 190+ countries; expected to close mid-2027.
Payoneer announced plans to launch stablecoin capabilities embedded within its platform, powered by Bridge.
Payoneer filed an application with the OCC to establish PAYO Digital Bank, N.A., a U.S. national trust bank charter to support its stablecoin strategy.

Payoneer acquired Dublin-based workforce management startup Boundless for $13M (plus up to $4M earn-out), and separately received in-principle authorization as a Payment Aggregator-Cross Border (PA-CB) in India.
Payoneer launched a partnership with Stripe to enhance and expand its Checkout offering, combining Stripe's technology with Payoneer's local market expertise.

Corpay added blockchain-based settlement through J.P. Morgan Kinexys and BVNK, extending its multi-rail cross-border platform with 24/7 stablecoin and tokenized-fiat disbursements across select corridors.

Mastercard and Corpay launched a strategic partnership: Mastercard made a $300M minority investment (~3% equity stake, $10.7B enterprise valuation) in Corpay's cross-border business, and Corpay became the exclusive provider of large-ticket cross-border payments and currency risk management to Mastercard's financial institution customers.
Corpay and Mastercard extended near-real-time payments to 22 new markets across Asia, Europe, Middle East, Africa, and Latin America.
Corpay completed Mastercard's $300M minority investment into its cross-border business, targeting first customer conversions from Q1 2026.

Corpay closed its acquisition of Alpha (adding ~$55M in Q4 revenue) and, with TPG, completed acquisition of a 34% stake in AvidXchange, expanding its mid-market AP automation and cross-border risk management footprint.
